body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The big story this Monday is a farewell — Shafter gathered at Minter Field over the weekend to remember Ronald Pierce, the museum's longtime chairman who spent decades keeping the airfield's history alive. Conditions outside are calm and warm: 61° at Meadows Field right now, a high near 86° this afternoon, no active weather alerts, and air quality sitting at a moderate 52.

## The Kern Overnight

Kern County dispatch logged 42 incidents between 7 p.m. and just past 5 a.m., and fires made up the largest share of them — 11 in all. Three were logged as structure fires, at 7:37, 8:44 and 4:25 this morning; the rest came in as fires of varying description, including one on South Bliss Street, one on South Chester Avenue, one on Lake Street, and a car fire on Olive Drive just after midnight that followed a crash near Highway 99.

Crashes and traffic accounted for six calls. A crash involving a Nissan was reported on Harris Road around 8:31 p.m., and a tow was requested after a collision damaged a guardrail in the 2 a.m. hour. A hit-and-run involving two vehicles came in a couple of minutes later, and officers responded to a crash on Gosford Road at 5:16 a.m.

Four weapons and assault calls were logged. Minor injuries were reported after a fight at Stockdale and River early in the evening, and an assault involving a knife possibly being used was reported at the Navigation Center late in the night. Two shootings were logged, at 9:03 and 11:16 p.m. Medical and overdose calls numbered five, including a person with a traumatic injury at Cherry Acres. Officers also ran four probation checks and answered four welfare calls. Details on all of these remain limited this morning, and we'll pass along anything more specific as it's confirmed.

## Today's weather

It's 61° at Meadows Field to start the day, on the way to a high near 86° — a warm one for mid-October, so plan on water if you're working outside. The low tonight drops to around 54°. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are being reported. Air quality is moderate at 52, which is fine for most of us but worth noting if you're sensitive to smoke or dust. Otherwise, a quiet, clear October day across the valley.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that Shafter said goodbye to Ronald Pierce on Sunday, and the send-off fit the man.** Dozens gathered at Minter Field Air Museum for a celebration of life that included a flyover, honoring the museum's longtime chairman, who died Sept. 4 after a short illness at 89. A Shafter native, Pierce first knew the airfield as a child while his father worked there during World War II, and from the early 2000s on he shared that history with students and visitors. Friends took the open mic to remember his early-morning dashes to the museum and his anniversary phone calls reminding other husbands to do right by their wives.

**According to 23ABC, Felicita Park in Arvin has finished its first major renovation, and it took only four months.** The city was awarded a donation of more than $56,000 in late spring, and the park at Felicita Road and Rayo de la Luna Drive now has exercise equipment, new benches and solar lights. Gustavo Aguirre of the Center on Race, Poverty, and the Environment said residents had waited years for lighting and improvements, and park-goers told the station the free equipment makes a fitness routine possible for neighbors who couldn't otherwise afford one.

**KGET 17 reports that tributes are still coming in for Bobby Rocha, the East Bakersfield High School athletic trainer who was taken from Friday night's football game by ambulance.** The game against Foothill stopped with less than two minutes left before halftime, and players, coaches and cheerleaders from both schools gathered at midfield to pray; officials declared Foothill the winner. Foothill's football program posted a tribute saying its "family is heartbroken," and Bakersfield College held a moment of silence before its homecoming game Saturday.

**Bakersfield Now reports that a boil water notice has been issued for parts of Bear Valley Springs amid power shutoff issues.** Residents in the affected area should boil tap water before drinking or cooking until the notice is lifted. We'll share any update on the notice's scope or timeline as soon as it's announced.

**KGET 17 also reports that a pedestrian suffered major injuries in a collision in Oildale, according to the California Highway Patrol.** Few details were available Monday morning, and the CHP's investigation is ongoing.

## Something good

The Via Arté chalk festival turned a Bakersfield parking lot into an open-air gallery over the weekend, with local artists and neighbors working side by side to fill the pavement with color for anyone who wanted to stroll through. It's the kind of event that costs nothing to enjoy and makes a plain stretch of asphalt feel like somewhere worth lingering — a good reminder that a lot of the art in this town shows up where you least expect it, and washes away with the next rain.

## Coming up this week

It's a busy week at City Hall. Tuesday starts early with the Historic Preservation Commission at 10 a.m., followed by the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2 p.m. and a special meeting of the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee, also at 2 p.m. Wednesday brings two City Council sessions — a 3:30 p.m. meeting and a 5:15 p.m. meeting — so check the agendas if you're tracking a particular item.

At the Fox Theater, the Cults & Classics series screens *Psycho* tonight, Switchfoot brings the Forever Now Tour with special guest Anberlin on Wednesday, comedian Henry Cho performs his Empty Nest Tour on Friday, and Saturday offers a double bill: Fred Armisen's "Comedy for Musicians But Everyone is Welcome" and the BLADE RAVE, both at the Fox. And if you're planning further out, season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics run are on sale now.

Have a good Monday, and we'll see you back here tomorrow.

top.title: Shafter remembers Ronald Pierce, Minter Field Air Museum chairman who spent decades preserving its history
